subject: Post-demo readout and recommended experiment plan: open models vs baseline
messages:
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Ruiz <alex.ruiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo readout and recommended experiment plan: open models vs baseline

Alex—thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our discovery + demo (short and actionable):

Summary of fit observations
- Primary goal: reduce question-answer latency in the customer support assistant while preserving accuracy on regulatory answer sets (policy + compliance).
- Current proprietary baseline (FinLyticsBERTPro v2 served on CPU) has good precision on short factual lookups but struggles with multi-turn context and follow-up clarifications.
- During the demo, we saw the open models provide much better contextual continuity but with variable hallucination rates on the policy domain.

Recommended models to trial (initial):
- Open-model candidate A: Mistral-Instruct-30B (fp16) — strong for instruction-following and lower per-token cost on Redwood hosted GPUs.
- Open-model candidate B: Llama-2-Chat-70B quant (4-bit Q4_K_M) — higher throughput with reasonable quality on long-context threads.
- Proprietary baseline: FinLyticsBERTPro v2 (current prod) — we will use as the control arm.

Acceptance thresholds to gate progression (proposed):
- Intent extraction / NER micro-F1 >= 0.82 (within 3% of baseline)
- End-to-end answer accuracy (policy citations) >= baseline - 2 percentage points
- Hallucination rate < 1.5% on the supplied gold-reference set (we will use the 1,200 annotated examples you mentioned)
- Latency: P95 inference latency < 800ms for the synchronous ticket-level call (target for Dedicated pool)

Experiment plan (high level)
1) Prep: we will run a 2-week A/B pilot across 1k daily queries (random split) using the three arms. We'll use identical prompt bundles and sampling configs for fairness.
2) Metrics: automated scoring (exact match / BLEU-style for short facts), human review for hallucination sampling, and token-level cost reporting.
3) Safety/regression: we will run the Redwood "regression guard" on prompt suites you shared and add a focused hallucination test.
4) Rollout gates: pass acceptance thresholds above, then can promote the winning open-model to a canary (10% traffic) for 48–72 hours before full swap.

Attachments included: finlytics-benchmark-results.csv (starter baseline metrics), prompt-bundle-v1.jsonl (initial prompt set we used in demo), and a short experiment plan PDF.

Next steps (action owners + dates)
- Alexandra: confirm the 1,200 annotated examples and share the secure S3 link by EOD Thu (4/29).
- Procurement: flag any required contract/PO lead time so we can align pilot start dates.
- Redwood (Neha): produce the experiment config + expected cost delta for open candidates by Fri (4/30).
- Redwood (Markus): schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff with your engineering team for the week of May 3.

If those timelines look reasonable I'll queue the experiment and send the pilot kick-off invite. Appreciate the thorough discussion today — we think there is a clear path to match or beat your baseline on the key metrics while reducing token costs.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo readout and recommended experiment plan: open models vs baseline

Alexandra — quick technical note and concrete config suggestions for the pilot. Pasting the core experiment steps so your engs can copy: 

Pilot config (example)
- Traffic split: 34% baseline (BERTPro), 33% Mistral-30B, 33% Llama2-Chat-70B-quant
- Prompt bundle: prompt-bundle-v1.jsonl (attached) with two canned clarifying-turn templates; do NOT apply system instructions that suppress citation output for the first pass.
- Sampling: greedy for NER/intent extraction tasks; nucleus p=0.9 with temperature 0.2 for assistant answer generation to match determinism.
- Logging: token-level cost + request trace id (Redwood trace_id) + full prompt/response stored in a secure bucket (retention 30 days for pilot)

Evaluation suite
- Automated: exact-match on 600 shorter lookups, macro-F1 on a 400-example NER set, BLEU/ROUGE-lite on 200 longer policy responses.
- Manual: 200 random samples stratified by category with a 3-person human review panel using the hallucination rubric we discussed.

Safety & regression guard
- We will run the Redwood regression guard across your compliance prompt suite nightly during pilot. Any drop >2% on the regression lead metric triggers a rollback to baseline.

Estimated incremental cost (pilot, 14 days):
- Mistral-30B: ~$1,800 total (hosted)
- Llama2-Chat-70B quant: ~$2,700 total (hosted)
- Logging/storage + human review: ~$950
- Note: these are estimates; Markus will provide a dedicated capacity quote if you prefer predictable P95 SLOs.

Deliverables by Friday (4/30): experiment config JSON, cost delta spreadsheet, and a sanitized prompt bundle for your team to audit.

If procurement can get the DPA template over I can loop Legal for a quick stamp.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
